paragraphs.text: But speak thou the things which befit the sound doctrine:
paragraphs.original: Σὺ δὲ λάλει ἃ πρέπει τῇ ὑγιαινούσῃ διδασκαλίᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: Sy de lalei ha prepei tē hygiainousē didaskalia.

paragraphs.text: that aged men be temperate, grave, sober-minded, sound in faith, in love, in patience:
paragraphs.original: πρεσβύτας νηφαλίους εἶναι, σεμνούς, σώφρονας, ὑγιαίνοντας τῇ πίστει, τῇ ἀγάπῃ, τῇ ὑπομονῇ.
paragraphs.translit: presbytas nēphalious einai, semnous, sōphronas, hygiainontas tē pistei, tē agapē, tē hypomonē.

paragraphs.text: that aged women likewise be reverent in demeanor, not slanderers nor enslaved to much wine, teachers of that which is good;
paragraphs.original: Πρεσβύτιδας ὡσαύτως ἐν καταστήματι ἱεροπρεπεῖς, μὴ διαβόλους μηδὲ οἴνῳ πολλῷ δεδουλωμένας, καλοδιδασκάλους,
paragraphs.translit: Presbytidas hōsautōs en katastēmati hieroprepeis, mē diabolous mēde oinō pollō dedoulōmenas, kalodidaskalous,

paragraphs.text: that they may train the young women to love their husbands, to love their children,
paragraphs.original: ἵνα σωφρονίζωσι τὰς νέας φιλάνδρους εἶναι, φιλοτέκνους,
paragraphs.translit: hina sōphronizōsi tas neas philandrous einai, philoteknous,

paragraphs.text: [to be] sober-minded, chaste, workers at home, kind, being in subjection to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed:
paragraphs.original: σώφρονας, ἁγνάς, οἰκουργούς, ἀγαθάς, ὑποτασσομένας τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν, ἵνα μὴ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ βλασφημῆται.
paragraphs.translit: sōphronas, hagnas, oikourgous, agathas, hypotassomenas tois idiois andrasin, hina mē ho logos tou theou blasphēmētai.

paragraphs.text: the younger men likewise exhort to be sober-minded:
in all things showing thyself an ensample of good works; in thy doctrine [showing] uncorruptness, gravity,
paragraphs.original: περὶ πάντα σεαυτὸν παρεχόμενος τύπον καλῶν ἔργων, ἐν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ ἀφθορίαν, σεμνότητα,
paragraphs.translit: peri panta seauton parechomenos typon kalōn ergōn, en tē didaskalia aphthorian, semnotēta,

paragraphs.text: sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of us.
paragraphs.original: λόγον ὑγιῆ ἀκατάγνωστον, ἵνα ὁ ἐξ ἐναντίας ἐντραπῇ μηδὲν ἔχων λέγειν περὶ ἡμῶν φαῦλον.
paragraphs.translit: logon hygiē akatagnōston, hina ho ex enantias entrapē mēden echōn legein peri hēmōn phaulon.

paragraphs.text: [Exhort] servants to be in subjection to their own masters, [and] to be well-pleasing [to them] in all things; not gainsaying;
paragraphs.original: Δούλους ἰδίοις δεσπόταις ὑποτάσσεσθαι ἐν πᾶσιν, εὐαρέστους εἶναι, μὴ ἀντιλέγοντας,
paragraphs.translit: Doulous idiois despotais hypotassesthai en pasin, euarestous einai, mē antilegontas,

paragraphs.text: not purloining, but showing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.
paragraphs.original: μὴ νοσφιζομένους, ἀλλὰ πᾶσαν πίστιν ἐνδεικνυμένους ἀγαθήν, ἵνα τὴν διδασκαλίαν τὴν τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν θεοῦ κοσμῶσιν ἐν πᾶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: mē nosphizomenous, alla pasan pistin endeiknymenous agathēn, hina tēn didaskalian tēn tou sōtēros hēmōn theou kosmōsin en pasin.

paragraphs.text: For the grace of God hath appeared, bringing salvation to all men,
paragraphs.original: Ἐπεφάνη γὰρ ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ σωτήριος πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις
paragraphs.translit: Epephanē gar hē charis tou theou sōtērios pasin anthrōpois

paragraphs.text: instructing us, to the intent that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly and righteously and godly in this present world;
paragraphs.original: παιδεύουσα ἡμᾶς, ἵνα ἀρνησάμενοι τὴν ἀσέβειαν καὶ τὰς κοσμικὰς ἐπιθυμίας σωφρόνως καὶ δικαίως καὶ εὐσεβῶς ζήσωμεν ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι,
paragraphs.translit: paideuousa hēmas, hina arnēsamenoi tēn asebeian kai tas kosmikas epithymias sōphronōs kai dikaiōs kai eusebōs zēsōmen en tō nyn aiōni,

paragraphs.text: looking for the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ;
paragraphs.original: προσδεχόμενοι τὴν μακαρίαν ἐλπίδα καὶ ἐπιφάνειαν τῆς δόξης τοῦ μεγάλου θεοῦ καὶ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: prosdechomenoi tēn makarian elpida kai epiphaneian tēs doxēs tou megalou theou kai sōtēros hēmōn Iēsou Christou,

paragraphs.text: who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a people for his own possession, zealous of good works.
paragraphs.original: ὃς ἔδωκεν ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἵνα λυτρώσηται ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ πάσης ἀνομίας καὶ καθαρίσῃ ἑαυτῷ λαὸν περιούσιον, ζηλωτὴν καλῶν ἔργων.
paragraphs.translit: hos edōken heauton hyper hēmōn hina lytrōsētai hēmas apo pasēs anomias kai katharisē heautō laon periousion, zēlōtēn kalōn ergōn.

paragraphs.text: These things speak and exhort and reprove with all authority. Let no man despise thee.
paragraphs.original: Ταῦτα λάλει καὶ παρακάλει καὶ ἔλεγχε μετὰ πάσης ἐπιταγῆς· μηδείς σου περιφρονείτω.
paragraphs.translit: Tauta lalei kai parakalei kai elenche meta pasēs epitagēs· mēdeis sou periphroneitō.
